text.title: llamaindex-ingestion-pipeline Core Rules
text.summary: Rules for LlamaIndex IngestionPipeline: composition, splitter choice, metadata extractors, vector-store persistence.

rule.statement: Always pass a docstore (SimpleDocumentStore or RedisDocumentStore) to IngestionPipeline. Without it, every run re-embeds the whole corpus.
rule.rationale: Docstore + content-hash dedup turns re-ingestion into a no-op when corpus unchanged.

rule.statement: Pick SentenceSplitter for structured/repetitive content (lists, FAQs, code); SemanticSplitterNodeParser for narrative prose.
rule.rationale: SemanticSplitter on structured docs over-splits into thousands of tiny nodes.

rule.statement: Run TitleExtractor + SummaryExtractor in the pipeline so retrieval has metadata handles. Without metadata you cannot filter or rerank by source.
rule.rationale: Metadata-aware retrieval lifts recall measurably on heterogeneous corpora.

rule.statement: Set num_workers ≥ 4 in IngestionPipeline.run for LLM-based extractors. Default sequential mode runs Nx slower.
rule.rationale: Metadata extractors are LLM calls; parallelism gives linear speedup until rate-limited.

rule.statement: Persist via StorageContext.from_defaults(persist_dir=...) AFTER pipeline.run; call storage_context.persist() before exit.
rule.rationale: In-memory stores die on restart; persistence is a single call you must not skip.

rule.statement: Hash document bodies for doc_id (not file path). Path-based IDs cause double-indexing on refactor.
rule.rationale: A repo reorganization re-embedded the entire corpus under new paths; cost spike to $40 for what should have been free.

rule.statement: For corpora over 100K nodes, use a hosted vector store (Pinecone, Weaviate, pgvector). In-memory Chroma is fine for dev only.
rule.rationale: In-memory cannot survive horizontal scaling or pod restarts in production.

rule.statement: Batch ingestion runs with chunked reads (do not load whole corpus into RAM). Use IngestionPipeline.run(documents=batch, in_place=False) per chunk.
rule.rationale: All-in-RAM ingestion OOMs at low single-digit GB corpus sizes.

rule.statement: When doc_count is high (tens of thousands of documents, at or past the 100K-node line in r7) AND update_frequency is continuous (daily or more, with documents also being removed), the ingestion-spec MUST run IngestionPipeline against a hosted vector store (r7) with a shared remote docstore (RedisDocumentStore or equivalent, not SimpleDocumentStore on local disk), docstore_strategy set to UPSERTS_AND_DELETE so deleted sources are purged from the vector store, doc_id derived from a content hash (r6), num_workers at least 4 for the extractors (r4), and batched runs over chunked reads (r8). Splitter is SentenceSplitter unless the profile is narrative prose AND embedding_budget_usd covers SemanticSplitterNodeParser (r2). A local-only docstore or a full-corpus rebuild per update is forbidden on this branch.

rationale.source: LlamaIndex documentation (IngestionPipeline document management, DocstoreStrategy, Redis docstore)

rule.rationale: With daily updates the dedup state is the product: a docstore on one pod's disk means every other worker re-embeds everything (fm-01), and the default upsert strategy never deletes, so removed documents keep answering queries for months. Content-hash IDs are what make the strategy survive a path refactor (fm-04).

rule.statement: When doc_count is high BUT update_frequency is periodic (weekly or less), the ingestion-spec MUST run IngestionPipeline with a SimpleDocumentStore attached and persisted next to the vector store via pipeline.persist(persist_dir) / IngestionPipeline.load(persist_dir) (r1, r5), the default upsert strategy keyed on content-hash doc_id (r6), a hosted vector store (r7), batched runs (r8) and TitleExtractor + SummaryExtractor with num_workers at least 4 (r3, r4). The fm-01 detector is part of the spec: a re-run on an unchanged corpus MUST cost near zero embed calls, otherwise the docstore is not wired.

rationale.source: LlamaIndex documentation (IngestionPipeline document management and persistence)

rule.rationale: At this size a re-embed is a real bill (the Applies-If floor is $10 per build), and the only thing standing between a weekly refresh and a weekly full rebuild is a docstore that survives the run. A local SimpleDocumentStore is sufficient here because a periodic job runs in one process; the Redis upgrade in r-advanced is for concurrent, continuous ingestion.

rule.statement: When doc_count is low (hundreds to a few thousand documents, above the 100-doc Skip-If floor), the ingestion-spec MUST still use IngestionPipeline rather than VectorStoreIndex.from_documents: SimpleDocumentStore attached and persisted to a local persist_dir together with the index (r1, r5), SentenceSplitter as the node parser (r2), TitleExtractor + SummaryExtractor run once with num_workers at least 4 (r3, r4), and content-hash doc_id (r6). A hosted vector store, a remote docstore and SemanticSplitterNodeParser are NOT added on this branch; the local persisted index is the deliverable.

rationale.source: LlamaIndex documentation (IngestionPipeline, storing and loading an index)

rule.rationale: The small-corpus trap is not scale, it is habit: the one-liner that re-embeds on every restart gets copied into the next project (fm-01). The pipeline shape costs nothing extra at this size and is what makes the metadata handles (fm-03) and the dedup exist at all, while hosted infrastructure would be pure operational weight.
